channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: Astronomers find the real sky inside Van Gogh's Starry Night
item.description: A new astronomical analysis matches the painting's crescent moon, Venus and five central stars to the pre-dawn sky over Saint-Rémy around July 22, 1889. Researchers say the pattern aligns with the Hyades cluster in Taurus, suggesting Van Gogh grounded the famous scene in observation.

item.title: Minnesota passerby leaps aboard a runaway bus and saves 18 children
item.description: Ebro Ahmed saw a St. Paul school bus moving with its doors open while the driver appeared to be having a seizure. He ran alongside, jumped aboard, pulled the parking brake and protected the driver until paramedics arrived, keeping all 18 students safe.

item.title: Chiricahua becomes America's 64th national park
item.description: Arizona's former Chiricahua National Monument has been elevated to national-park status, protecting 12,000 acres of volcanic rock spires, balanced stones and converging desert, grassland and forest habitats. The designation also recognizes the landscape's deep importance to Chiricahua Apache history.

item.title: Three Italian friends turn a lost wedding ring into a Tolkien quest
item.description: Three friends spent days searching a fast Italian stream for an Irish tourist's lost wedding ring, finally finding it with snorkeling gear. They then flew to Ireland dressed as hobbits to return the 'precious' in person, earning a tour, dinner and three new lifelong friends.

item.title: A first-grade positivity ritual spreads across a Kansas school
item.description: Teacher Tyler Richards ends each day with his first-graders reciting affirmations such as 'I am kind' and 'I can do hard things.' The practice proved so popular at Rex Elementary in Haysville that other classes adopted it and students began suggesting their own variations.

item.title: Solar shade nearly triples the weight of Italian grape bunches
item.description: A University of Bari vineyard study found grape bunches grown beneath solar panels weighed nearly three times as much as those in full sun. The partial shade also produced longer shoots, less heat stress and lower irrigation needs while the panels generated electricity.

item.title: Senior dog surrendered for euthanasia finds a new family
item.description: A healthy senior dog surrendered to a New Jersey shelter with a request that she be euthanized instead found a new home. Tillie, about 12, was adopted by a couple who already have a 12-year-old dog; her new family says she is settling in well.

item.title: Kitten named Freeway reaches safety after dodging interstate traffic
item.description: A driver stopped on Interstate 93 near Boston and rescued a seven-week-old black kitten weaving through traffic. The Animal Rescue League named her Freeway and placed her in foster care, where she will gain weight before becoming available for adoption.

item.title: Japan launches a five-year mission to bring home soil from Phobos
item.description: Japan's MMX spacecraft has begun a five-year voyage to Mars' moon Phobos. After arriving in 2027, it is designed to deploy a rover, collect at least 10 grams of material and return the first sample from a Martian moon to Earth in 2031.

item.title: Native wildlife rebounds after rats and pigs leave a Samoan island
item.description: A year after community-led teams removed invasive rats and feral pigs from Nu'utele, native seedlings carpet parts of the forest, giant taro is growing again and vulnerable birds are nesting. Conservationists also found a land-crab species not previously recorded on the island.

item.title: Strangers rally around an 86-year-old's 39-year boat project
item.description: Dale began welding a 62-foot steel boat in his Texas yard in 1987, hoping to sail it to Alaska. Three visiting Britons shared his story and started a fundraiser; more than 1,500 donors quickly contributed over $41,000 to help finish the vessel, move it down a steep hill and launch it.

item.title: A simpler process recovers 98 percent of used acrylic glass
item.description: ETH Zurich researchers devised a solvent-free method that turns used acrylic glass back into pure building blocks at roughly half the heat older methods require. It recovered up to 98 percent of the material, even from dyed or impure samples, and can work with existing industrial equipment.

item.title: Ten-year-old dog returns after a month alone in Yellowstone
item.description: Luna, a Jack Russell terrier, survived more than a month among Yellowstone's bears, wolves and freezing nights after escaping a cabin. Volunteer Katie Boucher and one of Luna's owners finally found her in a live trap baited with scraps from a family shirt and pillowcase. She was underweight but alert and ready for home.

item.title: Texas barber returns $128,514 left atop an ATM
item.description: An anonymous Lewisville barber found a cash-stuffed bag and 19 checks on a bank ATM, then immediately called police. Investigators traced the $128,514 to Bank of America after a repair technician apparently forgot it. The bank recovered every dollar, and police plan to honor the finder privately at his request.

item.title: Students turn a staged cafeteria fight into a principal's birthday surprise
item.description: Georgia principal Bobby Davis raced toward what looked like a cafeteria brawl, only for the crowd to shout “Happy Birthday.” The organizer was De'Zayviun Watkins, a 17-year-old who credits Davis with helping him control his anger and discover poetry, music and a career goal. The prank became a heartfelt thank-you to a mentor.
